correctness.rationale: For k=2, a JR witness is exactly absence of an available supporter set containing ≥q uncovered voters. If n odd any committee containing a q-support candidate satisfies JR; if n even the distinct-q-support-set vs common-set/complement coverage dichotomy gives the exact DR feasibility test. A case split by supporter sizes proves that any JR non-DR pair has a permitted quota-deviation-decreasing one-candidate swap while a DR pair exists; the integer deviation potential then terminates at DR. For k=3, q=2, six-voter five-candidate witness with supports a={1,2,3,4},b={3,5},c={4,5},d={2,6},e={5,6}: {b,c,d} is DR; {a,b,e} is JR and Local DR but not DR because both improving a→c,d break JR. Independent direct JR/swap enumerator confirms exact witness. The finite check is only a witness; k2 unlimited proof is the case analysis.
